Q2.
X is a Canadian software company founded in 1984, specializing in secure communications and the Internet of Things (IoT).
The brand is best known for its flagship product, Y.
Over time, the company became so strongly associated with Y that it was widely recognized by the product name itself in major markets. As a result, in 2013, the company rebranded itself to match its flagship product, Y.
Y was once considered one of the most effectively christened products in the technology industry, dominating the US market with more than 40% share before gradually “losing the signal” and eventually ceasing production in 2016.
Identify X and Y.
Fun fact- The term "CrackBerry" was coined in the mid-2000s, referencing the addictive nature of always-on work communication. Users were constantly glued to their devices to check emails.

Q3.
On July 5, 1994, Y was officially founded under the name X by a young Princeton graduate in a garage at his rented home in Bellevue, Washington.
The original name X was derived from a shortened form of a magical expression resembling _______ .
However, it was frequently misheard as “cadaver,” which carried an undesirable connotation for a consumer-facing brand.
Today, Y is regarded as one of the most influential economic and cultural forces in the world, and is among the most valuable brands globally.
Seeking a stronger identity, the founder decided to rebrand and specifically chose a name starting with “A” to ensure top placement in early internet directory listings. X was subsequently renamed to Y.
Identify X and Y.
